unread_leads.cell: (e) low-grade and high-grade glioma: tumor center (ADC1) and tumor edema (ADC2), 1.5 T
unread_leads.reason: Open full text was read. Table 2 ('... with scale of 10-3 mm2/s') gives for tumor edema (ADC2) low grade: mean 1.5, median 1.61, 95% CI 1.47–1.70; high grade: mean 1.4, median 1.41, CI 1.34–1.47; and for ADC1 low grade mean 1.2, median 1.29, CI 1.26–1.33; high grade mean 1.0, median 1.04. The means are printed with one decimal only and some are not consistent with the printed confidence intervals, and no SD is given, so no record was made. The definitions of ADC3 and ADC4 were not read.

unread_leads.cell: (a) human CSF, healthy subjects (T1-diffusion correlation spectra)
unread_leads.reason: Open full text was read. It gives only an approximate spectral peak position, not an ROI mean: 'the CSF peak ... has a narrower range of MD values centered around ≈ 3.0μm2/ms' (3.0 is also the upper limit of the analysis grid). Field strength not read. No record was made.

unread_leads.cell: (f) rat ex vivo fixed brain, 9.4 T, 2% and 4% PFA, scanned after 4 h at room temperature
unread_leads.reason: Open full text was read by search only. The only diffusivity numbers found are fitted MODEL values as a function of Gd-DTPA concentration ('The MD model for 4% PFA changed from 2.42×10−4 to 2.27×10−4 mm2/s, and in the 2% model from 2.25×10−4 to 2.14×10−4 mm2/s'); region and conditions were not clear from the snippet, so no record was made. A person should read this paper: it probably has the best-described ex vivo conditions.

unread_leads.cell: (a) CSF in the lateral ventricles (control patients with prior cancer and no evidence of disease)
unread_leads.reason: Open full text was read. Table 2 gives control-group ventricular ADC, for example right mid body 3.04 (0.38) and left mid body 3.15 (0.29), mean (SD), n=20. The table has no unit; the figure legend prints '× 10− 9 mm2/s', which is probably a misprint (the PubMed abstract text shows the cut-off values with the exponent lost: '3.22 × 10 m/s'). Field strength was not found. Controls are not healthy volunteers. No record was made.

unread_leads.citation: Helenius J et al. AJNR Am J Neuroradiol 2002;23:194-199
unread_leads.cell: (a) human normal brain 1.5 T, 36 regions and 4 age groups
unread_leads.reason: Free in PMC (PMC7975251) but the publisher does not allow XML download and my raw fetch was blocked. Only the ventricle and thalamus rows (all-subjects column) were taken through WebFetch. The remaining rows (white matter regions, caudate, putamen, cortex, per age group) are readable by a person in a browser. A single WebFetch call reported frontal white matter 0.70 ± 0.07 (left) / 0.71 ± 0.07 (right), caudate 0.76 ± 0.07, putamen 0.75 ± 0.06 (left) / 0.74 ± 0.06 (right); these were NOT recorded because they were seen in one call only.

unread_leads.reason: Direct in vivo versus formalin-fixed comparison in seven mice, seven ROIs (five white matter, two gray matter); the abstract says 'a significant decrease of Tr(D) was observed for all ROIs after fixation' but has no numeric diffusivity values; full text is on Wiley (paywall; the Wiley gateway was not used as instructed).

empty_cells: (c) human subcutaneous fat, in vivo: no record. Only a range from an abstract (Lehnert 2004, see unread_leads) and a qualitative statement plus a maximum in Steidle 2011. The bone-marrow-fat cell has 3 records (Steidle 2011, 1.5 T, tibial marrow).

(d) human blood IN VIVO: no source found (flow prevents a clean measurement). The 2 blood records are from ex vivo samples of human whole blood at body temperature (Funck 2018) and are marked condition 'ex vivo'.

(e) peritumoral VASOGENIC oedema named as such (for example around metastasis or meningioma): no record. Read, no value: PMC9334679 (edema in brain mass lesions), PMC3863968 (meningioma; tumour values only), PMC4248374 (no unit). The peritumoral records are 'peritumoral edema' of glioblastoma and of PCNSL (minimum ADC, 3 T) and 'tumor circumference hyperintensities' around glioma, metastasis and lymphoma (1.5 T).

(a) human cortical gray matter and white matter at 3 T from healthy volunteers with a full regional table: no machine-readable open source found. The 3 T normal values recorded are caudate and ventricles (Stieb 2020 abstract, medians) and corpus callosum / thalamus / caudate of 10 healthy controls (Exp Ther Med 2017).
(a) human CSF at 3 T: only medians from one abstract (Stieb 2020, IVIM-corrected). CSF at 1.5 T: Helenius 2002 table rows, read through WebFetch.
(f) mouse ex vivo: the scan temperature was not reported in the two sources (Wu 2013; Alomair 2015).
(f) rat ex vivo: one source (Wang 2018, 7 T, 4% PFA); scan temperature not stated.
(f) rat and mouse at other field strengths (for example 4.7 T, 9.4 T): no readable table found; most open papers show regional diffusivity only in figures.
